result.effect: 4.3% increase in explained variance; R2 = 0.205; Fchange(4, 153) = 9.477, p = 0.005

cells.quote: The hierarchical multiple regression analysis showed that students’ selection of relevant ideas from the texts contributed to their integration of information across texts over and above both reading fluency and reading comprehension skills.

D.treatment: social network analysis, particularly combined with content analysis

O.outcome_detail: understanding the nature and type of interactions between network members

cells.quote: Although the small number of included studies means that our systematic review should be considered preliminary, the evidence so far strongly suggests that SNA, particularly when combined with content analysis, can provide a detailed understanding of the nature and type of interactions between members of the network, allowing for optimisation of course design, composition of learner groups and identification of learners in danger of dropping out.
cells.note: The review reports a narrative pooled synthesis of 37 studies but does not state an explicit comparator, effect size, or equivalence/power analysis.

O.outcome_detail: SNP-based heritability of literacy, language and working-memory measures

cells.quote: Using Genome-wide Complex Trait Analysis (GCTA) software, GREML-based SNP-based heritability (GCTA SNP-h2) estimates for reading ﬂuency, spelling accuracy, phonemic awareness, listening comprehension, and non-word repetition ranged between 30% (SE = 0.06) and 50% (SE = 0.07) when assessed in unrelated children and adolescents from the general population, irrespective of phenotypic transformation (Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1).
cells.note: This was an observational genomic variance analysis, not an instructional comparison.

O.outcome_detail: proportion of SNP-based genetic variance captured by a shared factor

result.effect: shared factor captured 91%, 98%, and 97% of genetic variance for spelling, phonemic awareness, and passage reading, versus 44% and 53% for listening comprehension and non-word repetition

cells.quote: This corresponds to 91% (SE = 0.08), 98% (SE = 0.1), 97% (SE = 0.08), 44% (SE = 0.14), and 53% (SE = 0.14) of the genetic variance for each measure respectively (Supplementary Table 14). Thus, the majority of genetic variance across all traits (>90%) is captured by a shared genetic factor. Additional measurement-speciﬁc genetic inﬂuences, reﬂecting here trait-speciﬁc genetic variation, were estimated for listening comprehension and non-word repetition (Fig. 2a).
cells.note: The percentages correspond respectively to spelling, phonemic awareness, listening comprehension, non-word repetition, and passage reading as described immediately before the quoted sentence.

cells.quote: The shared genetic factor explained 27% (SE = 0.05) of the phenotypic variance for spelling accuracy, 31% (SE = 0.06) for phonemic awareness and 45% (SE = 0.07) for passage reading, but only 13% (SE = 0.04) for listening comprehension and 14% (SE = 0.04) for non-word repetition (Fig. 2b). This corresponds to 91% (SE = 0.08), 98% (SE = 0.1), 97% (SE = 0.08), 44% (SE = 0.14), and 53% (SE = 0.14) of the genetic variance for each measure respectively (Supplementary Table 14).
